scope: attempt to solve lastClientCommandString from the observed key shift

equation.observed: plain[i] = cipher[i] ^ 139 (what we decrypted with the constant key)

attempt.result_deltas: every delta came out in the 0x80..0x8f range, never in printable ASCII
attempt.conclusion: under the assumed plaintext, the implied command bytes are not printable, so either the plaintext header assumption is wrong or lastClientCommandString is not printable text

why_printable_matters.source: CODOL_Xor advances the key with command[index] << (i & 1) where command is (const byte*)client->lastClientCommandString with length sizeof(...) = 1024
why_printable_matters.implication: if the string were ordinary text, delta[even] would land in 0x20..0x7E; instead it lands at 0x80..0x8f, which is exactly 0x8b XOR small ASCII values
why_printable_matters.alternative: the field may contain a binary or UTF-16-ish representation, or the encoder may pass a pointer whose first bytes are not what we assume
